items.summary: Supreme Court Justice V Mohana on Friday drew parallels between law, music and cinema observing that all three involve interpretation and making sense of human experiences within their respective frameworks. Drawing a parallel between music and law, the judge said that while music has rules, rhythm structure and harmony which help an artist create music, so does law which has Constitution, legislation and procedure which provides a framework within which judges and lawyers work. " Law is not entirely different, the Constitution, legislation and procedure give us our framework, they tell us where the boundaries are and so judges are constantly trying to do something quite delicate; to interpret law faithfully while recognising that the world in which the law operates is constantly changing. The answer to why art matters to law is rather simple. We spend a great deal of time in law dealing with categories, principles and procedures. But behind every case is a person, behind every legal dispute is a human experience, " Justice Mohana said. However, with the latest spate of judicial appointments, every High Court in India is being helmed by a full time Chief Justice. The unusually large number of acting CJs over the last two months was largely the result of routine transfers, retirements, as well as a direct effect of the government's decision to expand the Supreme Court's sanctioned strength from 33 to 37 judges (excluding the Chief Justice of India) through the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Ordinance, 2026 and later, the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2026 . items.title: Legal Notes by Arvind Datar: Retrospectivity v. retroactivity and the need for a clear distinction
items.summary: What is the difference between a retrospective and a retroactive law? As this important question remains unanswered till date, this article suggests what the proper tests should be. Although most laws are prospective, it is settled that Parliament and the State legislatures have the competence to make laws with retrospective effect. These laws are declared to have come into effect on a date that is before the date of its enactment. Some laws have been declared to be effective decades earlier. The Finance Act, 1981 amended certain excise law provisions from 1944, while amendments made by the Finance Act, 2012 were to be effective from April 1, 2012. A “retroactive” law is also a law that is declared to be operative from an earlier date, but this category has a vital difference that is discussed a little later. The Supreme Court has referred to the two categories in several decisions. However, there is no clear distinction made in any of them. [See Shanti Conductors v.
